evals.prompt: I want to add a team invitation feature with email invites, expiration times, and invitation revocation.
evals.expected_output: The run should classify this as a new feature and multi-step behavior change, choose feature alignment flow, identify goals, non-goals, affected surfaces, acceptance criteria, and verification, ask only questions that affect behavior or risk, and avoid implementation until the behavior boundary is clear enough.
expectations: The run selects feature alignment flow for a multi-step feature
The run identifies goals, non-goals, affected behavior, acceptance criteria, and verification before implementation
The run asks only material questions or states assumptions before coding
The run does not require an external workflow backend before implementation

evals.prompt: The login page returns a 500 when I click submit. Please fix it.
evals.expected_output: The run should classify this as a lightweight bugfix, reproduce or inspect the failure before fixing, add a regression test first when practical, repair the smallest responsible boundary, and run targeted verification. It should not require feature alignment unless the bug reveals durable behavior or constraints.
expectations: The run selects the lightweight bugfix flow rather than full spec flow
The run investigates and reproduces before proposing a fix
The run adds or plans a regression test before implementation when practical

evals.prompt: The billing rule we agreed on just changed: trial users should also be included in usage statistics. Continue coding.
evals.expected_output: The run should detect a requirement change during coding, decide that it affects behavior, update task context or ask for alignment before continuing, and keep TDD and verification requirements in place.
expectations: The run detects that the prompt changes an approved requirement
The run updates task context or asks for alignment before continuing because behavior changed
The run keeps TDD and verification requirements after the requirement change

evals.prompt: This is simple, just change it directly: add an export data button to the user settings page.
evals.expected_output: The run should still recognize this as a user-visible feature, use a thin feature alignment flow, clarify button behavior, data scope, permissions, and verification, and not skip acceptance criteria just because the user called it simple.
expectations: The run does not skip behavior alignment merely because the user calls a feature simple
The run asks for or produces concise requirement alignment before coding

evals.prompt: $DDev has clarified the requirement boundary. Now call the coding flow to implement it and return evidence to DDev when done.
evals.expected_output: The run should recognize that it is being invoked as the DDev coding-flow module, implement according to the acceptance criteria and verification plan, use TDD or regression tests when practical, record tests and verification evidence, and return control to ddev rather than taking over delivery or durable memory.
expectations: The run treats spec-driven-coding as a DDev module when invoked by DDev
The run follows the acceptance criteria and verification plan
The run records tests or evidence before completion
The run returns lifecycle control to ddev after coding evidence
The run does not independently commit, push, or write durable memory unless requested
